exposure: planned delivery for a therapeutic anticoagulant window
delay between last low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) injection and neuraxial anaesthesia
outcome: deep venous thrombosis in the 6 weeks postpartum
cohort: 100 pregnant patients receiving prophylactic low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) who delivered after 24 weeks of gestation.
finding: Patients with a planned delivery for a therapeutic anticoagulant window had significantly higher access to neuraxial anaesthesia (100%) compared to those with spontaneous delivery (88.4%).
mod_finding: 11.5% of patients who went into spontaneous labour before a planned induction would not have received neuraxial anaesthesia due to an insufficient delay from the last LMWH injection.
gest_age: Delivery after 24 weeks of gestation; planned induced delivery between 38 and 39 weeks of gestation.
